meta.description: Community-maintained MLB National League injury tracking database. Machine-readable initial dataset covering Ronald Acuña Jr. (Atlanta Braves), Mookie Betts (Los Angeles Dodgers), and Freddie Freeman (Los Angeles Dodgers). Established as the foundational data layer for the nl-injury-tracker project.

primary_injury.type: Grade 1 left hamstring strain (second occurrence in 2026)
primary_injury.mechanism: Strained while running to first base against the Chicago White Sox in the bottom of the second inning
primary_injury.description: Acuña departed Tuesday night's game against the White Sox after attempting to beat out a ground ball to third base, a play he historically made effortlessly. He was placed on the 10-day IL the following day. This is the second time this specific injury has sent him to the IL in 2026 (first occurrence May 2026, only 15-day IL stint). The Braves have been cautious with rehabilitation given his extensive injury history.
primary_injury.notes: Braves manager Walt Weiss: 'I won't rule it out, but they've got his schedule mapped out for him.'

secondary_injuries.description: Suffered in Spring Training on March 3, 2026. Placed on 60-day IL. Rehab progressed steadily through April-May 2026. Rehab complete and no longer on IL.

rehab_location_history.details: FCL rehab including grand slam in 3rd rehab game (423 ft, 112.8 mph exit velo)
Rehab assignment with Gwinnett; played RF for first time July 19
rehab_location_history.games: First game July 18; RF debut July 19 (0-for-2, SF); second game July 21 (1-for-4, single)

rehabilitation_progress.activation_details: Target return for Braves homestand vs. San Diego Padres (4-game set starting July 20)

rehab_risk_factors: History of returning too early from ACL surgeries (2021 ACL-R, 2024 ACL-L)
Two hamstring strains in same season
Age 26 - still relatively young but积累了 significant trauma to left leg structures

latest_update.summary: Acuña cleared all rehab gates including outfield work for first time (July 19 at Triple-A Gwinnett). Expected MLB activation July 22-23 pending Braves management decision. Hit grand slam in FCL rehab game (423 ft, 112.8 mph exit velo) signaling full power return.

players.name: Mookie Betts
players.position: Shortstop / Third Base / Outfield / Designated Hitter

primary_injury.mechanism: Strained right oblique while running the bases against the Washington Nationals at Dodger Stadium
primary_injury.description: An MRI before his 10-day stint confirmed the oblique strain rather than a more serious issue. Betts was placed on the 10-day IL on April 5, 2026, and began rehab in the Dodgers' farm system with two games at Single-A in early May followed by two more at Triple-A Oklahoma City. He was activated from the 10-day IL on May 12, 2026, with Opening Day lefty Blake Snell also activated the same day. Before the injury, Betts had hit .179 with two home runs, seven runs batted in and three walks drawn after opening the season as the Dodgers' full-time shortstop.
primary_injury.return_details: Activated May 12, 2026; batted 2nd in return game vs. Giants; cautious return plan: Mon/Tue play, Wed off, then 2 of next 3

secondary_injuries.mechanism: Discomfort felt running bases against the Washington Nationals; initially suggested oblique strain but confirmed oblique strain from April rehabilitation resolved; current back stiffness unrelated to oblique
secondary_injuries.description: Dave Roberts confirmed Betts is day-to-day with lower back stiffness but NOT expected to land on IL. Conservative short rests rather than IL placement. Part of pattern of minor ailments managed day-to-day.
Resolved with treatment; Betts was only day-to-day after missing games July 2-3 due to wrist soreness.

secondary_injuries.mechanism: Suspected norovirus stomach illness during Tokyo exhibition series
secondary_injuries.description: Severe undiagnosed stomach illness in late March/July 2025 caused significant weight loss and inability to eat solid food. Blood work and medical tests returned normal. Betts lost appetite, vomiting after eating; treated with new medication. Returned to playing weight by spring 2026. Did not go on IL due to symptoms being non-specific and non-infectious in nature.

He recovered from a very scary fall into the Royals dugout on August 12 — the team described it as about dodging a bullet given how violent the fall looked.

comparison.all_stars_health: Freeman is the most durable and currently healthiest of the three tracked NL stars.
comparison.betts_recovery: Mookie Betts overcame the most mysterious and dangerous health scare of the three — the post-viral syndrome in 2025 that caused dramatic weight loss — and has returned to elite third base shortstop production.
comparison.acuna_injury_frequency: Acuña carries the heaviest injury load and requires the most cautious treatment of recurring left-body issues.

injury_compare.acuna: Highest frequency of injuries, recurring left-side issues, long-term severity
injury_compare.betts: Most dangerous non-injury health event (illness), diverse acute injuries resolved well
injury_compare.freeman: Chronic ankle issue, acute minor injuries managed well

Include date and source for any new information added

json_schema.player_id: string (unique identifier based on player name)
json_schema.name: string (full legal name)
json_schema.team: string (current team at time of data entry)
json_schema.current_injury: object with primary_injury and secondary_injuries arrays
json_schema.injury_history: array of objects with date, type, status, il_status, return_date
json_schema.latest_update: object with date, summary, sources array
json_schema.manager_quotes: array of objects with date, quote, speaker
